rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The questions refer to idols, which lack limbs with which to serve their worshippers.
rows.anchor: يعني أرجل يمشون بها في مصالحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols cannot walk to attend to their worshippers’ interests.
rows.anchor: يعني أرجل يمشون بها في مصالحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols lack hands with which to defend their worshippers.
rows.anchor: يعني في الدفع عنكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols cannot see their worshippers’ harms and benefits.
rows.anchor: يعني مضاركم من منافعكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols cannot hear worshippers’ calls and supplications.
rows.anchor: دعاءكم وتضرعكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worshipping a body that cannot benefit anyone is more blameworthy than worshipping one that can.
rows.anchor: أن من عبد جسما لا ينفع كان ألوم ممن عبد جسما ينفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People are superior to idols, so it is incoherent for them to worship beings beneath them.
rows.anchor: أنه عرفهم أنهم مفضلون عليها

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Remembering God inwardly means silently reciting behind the imam during prayer.
rows.anchor: ذكر القرءاة في الصلاة خلف الإمام سرا في نفسه قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It can mean remembrance in the heart, sustained reflection so one does not forget God’s favors that require obedience.
rows.anchor: ذكر بالقلب باستدامة الفكر حتى لا ينسى نعم الله الموجبة لطاعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It can mean remembrance on the tongue, either asking God in hope or magnifying Him through recitation.
rows.anchor: ذكره باللسان إما رغبة إليه في دعائه أو تعظيما له بالآية

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: The addressee is someone listening to the Qur’an, whether in prayer or during a sermon.
rows.anchor: المستمع للقرآن إما في الصلاة أو الخطبة , قاله ابن زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the Prophet is addressed, with the instruction applying generally to all morally responsible people.
rows.anchor: أنه خطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ومعناه عام في جميع المكلفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tadarruʿ means humility and reverence; khīfa means fear of God.
rows.anchor: التضرع فهو التواضع والخشوع , وأما الخيفة فمعناه مخافة منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means speaking quietly, whether remembrance is inward or on the tongue, according to the two readings above.
rows.anchor: يعني أسر القول إما بالقلب أو باللسان على ما تقدم من التأويلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation takes these times as morning and evening.
rows.anchor: فيه وجهان : أحدهما : بالبكر والعشيات

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Al-ghuduww is the end of dawn at the morning prayer and al-āsāl the late afternoon at ʿAṣr; Qatāda gives a similar view.
rows.anchor: آخر الفجر صلاة الصبح , والآصال آخر العشي صلاة العصر , قاله مجاهد , ونحوه عن قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not being heedless can mean not neglecting remembrance of God.
rows.anchor: يحتمل وجهين : أحدهما : عن الذكر . والثاني : عن طاعته

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Alternatively, it means not neglecting obedience to all of God’s commands and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: عن طاعته في كل أوامره ونواهيه , قاله الجمهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the first prostration of recitation in the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: وهذا أول سجدات التلاوة في القرآن

rows.speaker: كفار مكة
rows.claim: Meccan disbelievers objected, “What is the Merciful? Shall we prostrate to what you command?”; God then revealed this verse.
rows.anchor: وسبب نزولها ما قاله كفار مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If even the angels brought near submit with humility and longing, people are still more entitled to do so.
rows.anchor: إذا كانوا على هذه الحال في الخضوع والرغبة فأنتم بذلك أولى

none: A stray brace only; no commentary to record.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading is that they cease hostilities and make peace, so previous liability and punishment are forgiven.
rows.anchor: إن ينتهوا عن المحاربة إلى الموادعة يغفر لهم ما قد سلف من المؤاخذة والمعاقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading is that they cease disbelief by embracing Islam, so their previous sins are forgiven.
rows.anchor: إن ينتهوا عن الكفر بالإسلام يغفر لهم ما قد سلف من الآثام

words: وَإِن يَعُودُوا۟ فَقَدْ مَضَتْ سُنَّتُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
rows.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد والسدي
rows.claim: If they return to fighting, the precedent is Badr, where some were killed and others taken captive.
rows.anchor: وإن يعودوا إلى المحاربة فقد مضت سنة الأولين فيمن قتل يوم بدر وأسر , قاله الحسن ومجاهد والسدي

words: وَإِن يَعُودُوا۟ فَقَدْ مَضَتْ سُنَّتُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they return to disbelief, the precedent is the destruction God inflicted on earlier nations in this world.
rows.anchor: فقد مضت سنة الأولين من الأمم السالفة فيما أخذهم الله به في الدنيا من عذاب الاستئصال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: After Mecca’s conquest, the Prophet asked its people what they expected him to do; they appealed to his generosity, and he answered with Joseph’s words before this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : نزلت هذه الآية في أهل مكة بعد أن دخلها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عام الفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can mean that hypocrites join one another in hypocrisy.
rows.anchor: أن بعضهم يجتمع مع بعض على النفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they acquire hypocrisy from one another.
rows.anchor: أن بعضهم يأخذ نفاقه من بعض

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī says they follow one another’s religion.
rows.anchor: الكلبي : بعضهم على دين بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation takes reprehensible acts as everything reason rejects, such as shirk, and recognized good as everything good reason recognizes.
rows.anchor: المنكر كل ما أنكره العقل من الشرك , والمعروف : كل ما عرفه العقل من الخير

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says that in the Qur’an, recognized good means faith and reprehensible acts mean shirk.
rows.anchor: المعروف في كتاب الله تعالى كله الإيمان , والمنكر في كتاب الله تعالى كله الشرك , قاله أبو العالية

rows.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد
rows.claim: They withhold their hands from spending in God’s cause.
rows.anchor: يقبضونها عن الإنفاق في سبيل الله تعالى , قاله الحسن ومجاهد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says they withhold their hands from every good deed.
rows.anchor: يقبضونها عن كل خير , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: بعض المتأخرين
rows.claim: Some later commentators say they withhold their hands from fighting alongside the Prophet.
rows.anchor: عن الجهاد مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم , قاله بعض المتأخرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reported interpretation is that they refrain from raising their hands in supplication to God.
rows.anchor: يقبضون أيديهم عن رفعها في الدعاء إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They abandoned God’s command, so He abandoned them to the loss of His mercy.
rows.anchor: أي تركوا أمره فترك رحمتهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports 300 male and 170 female hypocrites in Medina.
rows.anchor: كان المنافقون بالمدينة من الرجال ثلاثمائة , ومن النساء سبعين ومائة امرأة

rows.speaker: مكحول عن أبي الدرداء
rows.claim: Via Makhūl, Abū al-Dardāʾ asks the Prophet about hypocrites; the Prophet lists lying, betrayal, broken promises, abusive quarrels, broken covenants, neglect of prayer, and little remembrance of God.
rows.anchor: مكحول عن أبي الدرداء أنه سأل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن صفة المنافق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: After the repentance of Abū Lubāba and his companions, they offered property as charity; the Prophet waited for a command, and this verse came down.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : لما نزل في أبي لبابة وأصحابه

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies the charity as a voluntary gift of property offered by them.
rows.anchor: الصدقة التي بذلوها من أموالهم تطوعا , قاله ابن زيد

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima identifies it as obligatory zakat; the wording says “from their wealth” because zakat is due only on some kinds of property.
rows.anchor: الزكاة التي أوجبها الله تعالى في أموالهم فرضا , قاله عكرمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The charity purifies their sins and makes their deeds grow in goodness.
rows.anchor: أي تطهر ذنوبهم وتزكي أعمالهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the command as asking forgiveness for them.
rows.anchor: استغفر لهم : قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī glosses it as praying for them.
rows.anchor: ادع لهم , قاله السدي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In a report through al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Ibn ʿAbbās glosses sakana as nearness to God.
rows.anchor: قربة لهم , قاله ابن عباس في رواية الضحاك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In a report through Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, Ibn ʿAbbās glosses it as mercy for them.
rows.anchor: رحمة لهم , رواه ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس أيضا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda glosses sakana as dignity and composure for them.
rows.anchor: وقار لهم , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba glosses it as reassurance for them.
rows.anchor: تثبت لهم , قاله ابن قتيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It can mean security for them, supported by a poet’s line saying a neighbor was a refuge when others were not.
rows.anchor: أمن لهم , ومنه قول الشاعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One legal view obligates the collector to pray for the donor, based on the command’s apparent wording.
rows.anchor: يجب على الآخذ الدعاء للمعطي اعتبارا بظاهر الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view recommends but does not require the prayer: God, not the collector, rewards the charity.
rows.anchor: لا يجب ولكن يستحب لأن جزاءها على الله تعالى لا على الآخذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third view requires prayer for a voluntary contribution but only recommends it for obligatory zakat.
rows.anchor: إن كانت تطوعا وجب على الآخذ الدعاء , وإن كانت فرضا استحب ولم يجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth view recommends prayer for a donor to the ruler but requires it for a poor recipient, who is not individually designated.
rows.anchor: إن كان آخذها الوالي استحب له الدعاء ولم يجب عليه , وإن كان آخذها الفقير وجب عليه الدعاء له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fifth view requires prayer for a donor to the ruler, as this displays obedience deserving thanks, but recommends it for a poor recipient.
rows.anchor: إن كان آخذها الوالي وجب , وإن كان الفقير استحب ولم يجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sixth view requires prayer if the donor asks for it and recommends it otherwise.
rows.anchor: إن سأل الدافع الدعاء وجب , وإن لم يسأل استحب ولم يجب

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي أوفى
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Awfā brought his people’s charity and asked the Prophet to pray for him; the Prophet prayed for the family of Abī Awfā.
rows.anchor: عبد الله بن أبي أوفى قال : أتيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بصدقات قومي

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid glosses God’s being on a straight path as His being upon the truth.
rows.anchor: على الحق , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: علي بن عيسى
rows.claim: ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā glosses it as God’s sound and well-ordered governance.
rows.anchor: على تدبير محكم , قاله علي بن عيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possible sense is the path of the afterlife, where people return to God for recompense and final judgment.
rows.anchor: أنه على طريق الآخرة في مصيركم إليه للجزاء وفصل القضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says Gabriel cried out against them.
rows.anchor: أن جبريل عليه السلام صاح بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says God caused a creature to cry out against them.
rows.anchor: أن الله تعالى أحدثها في حيوان صاح بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third account says God created the cry without a creature.
rows.anchor: أن الله تعالى أحدثها من غير حيوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the cry struck them at night, they were dead by morning.
rows.anchor: لأن الصيحة أخذتهم ليلا فأصبحوا منها هلكى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One sense is in their homes or lands, as in ordinary expressions naming tribal lands.
rows.anchor: في منازلهم وبلادهم , من قولهم هذه ديار بكر وديار ربيعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it means in the abode of this world, which is the home of all creation.
rows.anchor: في دار الدنيا لأنها دار لجميع الخلق

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
rows.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd glosses the word as lying dead overnight, since the cry struck at night.
rows.anchor: مبيتين , لأن الصحية كانت بياتا في الليل , قاله عبد الرحمن بن زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another gloss is that they were dead, from the sense of falling or remaining in a crouch.
rows.anchor: هلكى بالجثوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Juthūm can mean falling face down.
rows.anchor: أنه السقوط على الوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Juthūm can also mean sitting on one’s knees.
rows.anchor: أنه القعود على الركب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can mean it was as if they had never lived there.
rows.anchor: كأن لم يعيشوا فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it was as if they had never enjoyed its prosperity.
rows.anchor: كأن لم ينعموا فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One gloss is that Thamūd denied their Lord’s threat.
rows.anchor: كذبوا وعيد ربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another gloss is that they disbelieved God’s command.
rows.anchor: كفروا بأمر ربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The destruction annihilated Thamūd except Abū Ramḥān, who was in God’s sanctuary and was protected from the punishment.
rows.anchor: إلا رجلا منهم وهو أبو رمحان كان في حرم الله تعالى فمنعه الحرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Madyan here is the people of Shuʿayb.
rows.anchor: ومدين هم قوم شعيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says they are the sons of Madyan son of Abraham; the tribal ancestor’s name stands for his descendants, as with Muḍar.
rows.anchor: لأنهم بنو مدين بن إبراهيم , فقيل مدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account identifies Madyan as their city, whose name was used for its inhabitants for brevity.
rows.anchor: أن مدين اسم مدينتهم فنسبوا إليها ثم اقتصر على اسم المدينة تخفيفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Madyan may be a foreign name or, alternatively, an Arabic one.
rows.anchor: أنه اسم أعجمي . الثاني : أنه اسم عربي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If it is a city name, it may derive from madana, “to reside in a place,” with the yāʾ treated as extra.
rows.anchor: مدن بالمكان إذا أقام فيه , والياء زائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If it is a man’s name, it may derive from dānat, “to rule or possess,” with the mīm treated as extra.
rows.anchor: دينت أي ملكت والميم زائدمة , وهذا قول من زعم أنه اسم رجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuʿayb is a diminutive of shaʿb, which can mean a mountain path.
rows.anchor: شعيب فتصغير شعب وفيه ثلاثة أوجه : أحدها : أنه الطريق في الجبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another proposed sense of shaʿb is a great tribe.
rows.anchor: أنه القبيلة العظيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third proposal derives the name from repairing a broken vessel.
rows.anchor: أنه مأخوذ من شعب الإناء المكسور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though guilty of shirk, they also cheated in measures; belief calls them to abandon shirk and full measure forbids cheating.
rows.anchor: كانوا مع كفرهم أهل بخس وتطفيف فأمروا بالإيمان إقلاعا عن الشرك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan take “in good condition” to mean low prices.
rows.anchor: أنه رخص السعر , قاله ابن عباس والحسن

rows.speaker: قتادة وابن زيد
rows.claim: Qatāda and Ibn Zayd take it to mean wealth and worldly adornment.
rows.anchor: أنه المال وزينة الدنيا , قال قتادة وابن زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possible sense is abundant crops and earnings.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل تأويلا ثالثا : أنه الخصب والكسب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
rows.claim: On the low-price reading of “in good condition,” the warning can mean fear of high prices.
rows.anchor: غلاء السعر , وهو مقتضى قول ابن عباس والحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possibility is worldly punishment of total destruction.
rows.anchor: عذاب الاستصال في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning can also mean the punishment of the Fire in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: عذاب النار بالآخرة

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash glosses ṣalāt as recitation.
rows.anchor: قراءتك , قاله الأعمش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may mean Shuʿayb’s devotional prayer to God.
rows.anchor: صلاتك التي تصليها لله تعبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may mean his religion, which he was ordered to follow; ṣalāt’s root sense is following, as in the horse-racing term al-muṣallī.
rows.anchor: دينك الذي تدين به وأمرت باتباعه لأن أصل الصلاة الاتباع , ومنه أخذ المصلي في الخيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question can mean that Shuʿayb’s prayer calls him to their way.
rows.anchor: تدعوك إلى أمرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the question asks whether his prayer commands them to abandon the idols and images their ancestors worshipped.
rows.anchor: فيها أن تأمرنا أن نترك ما يعبد آباؤنا يعني من الأوثان والأصنام

words: أَوْ أَن نَّفْعَلَ فِىٓ أَمْوَٰلِنَا مَا نَشَٰٓؤُا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that their desired conduct was cheating in weights and measures.
rows.anchor: ما كانوا عليه من البخس والتطفيف

words: أَوْ أَن نَّفْعَلَ فِىٓ أَمْوَٰلِنَا مَا نَشَٰٓؤُا۟
rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم وسفيان الثوري
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam and Sufyān al-Thawrī say Shuʿayb commanded them to pay zakat, which they refused.
rows.anchor: الزكاة , كان يأمرهم بها فيمتنعون منها , قاله زيد بن أسلم وسفيان الثوري

words: أَوْ أَن نَّفْعَلَ فِىٓ أَمْوَٰلِنَا مَا نَشَٰٓؤُا۟
rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says Shuʿayb also forbade them from clipping coins.
rows.anchor: قطع الدراهم والدنانير لأنه كان ينهاهم عنه , قال زيد بن أسلم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says they called him wise and rightly guided sarcastically.
rows.anchor: قالوا ذلك استهزاء به , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reads the words as a denial: they mean Shuʿayb is neither forbearing nor rightly guided.
rows.anchor: معناه أنك لست بحليم ولا رشيد على وجه النفي , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن بحر
rows.claim: Ibn Baḥr says they sincerely concede Shuʿayb’s wisdom, then ask why he forbids them their desired conduct with their property.
rows.anchor: اعترفوا له بالحلم والرشد على وجه والحقيقة وقالوا أنت حليم رشيد

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk glosses the good provision as lawful wealth; Ibn ʿAbbās adds that Shuʿayb was very wealthy.
rows.anchor: المال الحلال , قاله الضحاك

rows.speaker: ابن عيسى
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĪsā says the good provision means prophethood.
rows.anchor: أنه النبوة , ذكره ابن عيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording omits a clause, understood as: would I turn away from worship despite this proof and provision?
rows.anchor: وفي الكلام محذوف وتقديره , أفأعدل مع ذلك عن عبادته

words: وَمَآ أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُخَالِفَكُمْ إِلَىٰ مَآ أَنْهَىٰكُمْ عَنْهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuʿayb will not do what he forbids them, just as he will not abandon what he commands.
rows.anchor: أي لا أفعل ما نهيتكم عنه كما لا أترك ما أمرتكم به

words: إِنْ أُرِيدُ إِلَّا ٱلْإِصْلَٰحَ مَا ٱسْتَطَعْتُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He intends only to act righteously as far as he can; ability conditions action, not intention.
rows.anchor: ما أريد إلا فعل الصلاح ما استطعت , لأن الاستطاعة من شرط الفعل دون الإرادة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid takes ināba as returning: “to Him I return.”
rows.anchor: أن الإنابة الرجوع ومعناه وإليه أرجع , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: عبيد الله بن يعلى
rows.claim: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Yaʿlā takes ināba as supplication: “to Him I pray.”
rows.anchor: أن الإنابة الدعاء , ومعناه وإليه أدعو , عبيد الله بن يعلى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the true call is the testimony “There is no god but God.”
rows.anchor: أن دعوة الحق لا إله إلا الله , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that God is the Real, so calling upon Him is the true call.
rows.anchor: هو الحق , فدعاؤه دعوة الحق

rows.speaker: بعض المتأخرين
rows.claim: Some later commentators identify the true call as sincere devotion in supplication.
rows.anchor: أن الإخلاص في الدعاء هي دعوة الحق , قاله بعض المتأخرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possible sense, fitting the context, is calling upon God in danger, when no one else is invoked; the next phrase concerns idols invoked besides Him.
rows.anchor: دعاؤه عند الخوف لأنه لا يدعى فيه إلا إياه , كما قال تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols neither answer their supplications nor hear their calls.
rows.anchor: أي لا يجيبون لهم دعاء ولا يسمعون لهم نداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water simile expresses despair of an answer; Arabs use reaching for water by hand as an example of striving for what cannot be attained.
rows.anchor: ضرب الله عز وجل الماء مثلا لإياسهم من إجابة دعائهم لأن العرب تضرب لمن سعى فيما لا يدركه مثلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū al-Hudhayl’s line compares a lost bond of affection to someone grasping water by hand.
rows.anchor: مثلا بالقابض الماء باليد , كما قال أبو الهذيل

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid compares the idolater to a thirsty person calling distant water toward his mouth, motioning with his hand but unable to attain it; the water does not answer or come.
rows.anchor: وما الماء ببالغ إليه , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās compares the idolater to a thirsty person reaching toward a reflection of water, deceived by a false impression that cannot bring it to his mouth.
rows.anchor: لكذب ظنه وفساد توهمه , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third explanation is someone stretching a hand toward water to grasp it, but getting nothing in his palm.
rows.anchor: كباسط كفه إلى الماء ليقبض عليه فلا يحصل في كفيه شيء منه

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says “water” means a well, its source; the example is reaching into a well without a rope, as the following poem indicates.
rows.anchor: المراد بالماء ها هنا البئر لأنها معدن للماء , وأن المثل كمن مد يده إلى البئر بغير رشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet’s line about an inherited well that he dug and lined supports al-Farrāʾ’s reading of water as a well.
rows.anchor: فإن الماء ماء أبي وجدي … وبئري ذو حفرت وذو طويت

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says believers prostrate willingly and disbelievers unwillingly.
rows.anchor: طوعا سجود المؤمن , وكرها سجود الكافر , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says some entered Islam willingly and others under threat of the sword.
rows.anchor: من دخل في الإسلام رغبة , { وكرها } من دخل فيه رهبة بالسيف , قاله ابن زيد

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī says long-standing Muslims have become accustomed to prostration, while new converts at first do it reluctantly until accustomed.
rows.anchor: من طالت مدة إسلامه فألف السجود , { وكرها } من بدأ بالإسلام حتى يألف السجود , حكاه ابن الأنباري

rows.speaker: بعض أصحاب الخواطر
rows.claim: Some people of spiritual insight say a person becomes humble in adversity but grows weary when blessings continue.
rows.anchor: بعض أصحاب الخواطر أنه إذا نزلت به المصائب ذل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each person’s shadow prostrates with him: the believer’s shadow willingly and the disbeliever’s unwillingly.
rows.anchor: ظل كل إنسان يسجد معه بسجوده , فظل المؤمن يسجد طائعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-āṣāl is a plural of aṣl, itself a plural of aṣīl; aṣīl is late afternoon from ʿAṣr until sunset.
rows.anchor: والآصال جمع أصل , والأصل جمع أصيل , والأصيل العشي وهو ما بين العصر والمغرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Dhuʾayb’s verse uses aṣāʾil for the late afternoons when one sits in the household’s courtyards.
rows.anchor: لعمري لأنت البيت أكرم أهله … وأقعد في أفيائه بالأصائل

none: A stray brace only; no commentary to record.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that each valley receives water according to what was allotted to it, whether little or much.
rows.anchor: يعني بما قدر لها من قليل أو كثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, small valleys flow in proportion to their smallness and large valleys to their size.
rows.anchor: الصغير من الأودية سال بقدر صغره , والكبير منها سال بقدر كبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain images the Qur’an’s universal good and lasting benefit; valleys are hearts that receive according to their capacity.
rows.anchor: فشبه القرآن بالمطر لعموم خيره وبقاء نفعه , وشبه القلوب بالأودية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the water is the Qur’an and the valleys are people’s hearts.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : { أنزل من السماء ماء } أي قرآنا { فسالت أودية بقدرها } قال : الأودية قلوب العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rābī means elevated.
rows.anchor: الرابي : المرتفع

words: فَأَمَّا ٱلزَّبَدُ فَيَذْهَبُ جُفَآءً وَأَمَّا مَا يَنفَعُ ٱلنَّاسَ فَيَمْكُثُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Useful water that remains represents truth; foam that vanishes without benefit represents falsehood.
rows.anchor: فالحق ممثل بالماء الذي يبقى في الأرض فينتفع به , والباطل ممثل بالزبد الذي يذهب جفاء لا ينتفع به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The adornment sought by heating metal means gold and silver.
rows.anchor: ابتغاء حلية } يعني الذهب والفضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The metal made for use means brass and copper.
rows.anchor: أو متاع } يعني الصفر والنحاس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Smelting produces dross like water’s foam: useless impurity departs as falsehood does, while the refined remainder is useful like truth.
rows.anchor: إذا سبك بالنار كان له خبث كالزبد الذي على الماء يذهب فلا ينتفع به كالباطل , ويبقى صفوة فينتفع به كالحق

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarīr glosses jufāʾ as separated or dispersed.
rows.anchor: يعني منشقا قاله ابن جرير

rows.speaker: ابن عيسى
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĪsā glosses it as cast away onto the earth’s surface.
rows.anchor: جافيا على وجه الأرض , قاله ابن عيسى

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Isḥāq glosses it as thrown away.
rows.anchor: الثالث : مرميا , قاله ابن إسحاق

rows.speaker: رؤية
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda heard Ruʾya read jafālan; he explains ajfalat al-qidr as the pot casting out its foam.
rows.anchor: سمع رؤية يقرأ : جفالا . قال أبو عبيدة : يقال أجفلت القدر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the phrase as enduring destruction.
rows.anchor: لهلاك دائم , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid glosses it as lying on a marked road.
rows.anchor: لبطريق معلم , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to the people of Lot’s towns and the people of the Thicket, Shuʿayb’s community.
rows.anchor: بقوله { وإنما } أهل مدائن قوم لوط وأصحاب الأيكة قوم شعيب
